title: Norwegian cultural participation is stabilizing unevenly: libraries recover while cinema and theatre remain below earlier levels
geography: Norway; representative population survey of physical and digital cultural participation

observations.period: 2025 Cultural Barometer; comparison with 2016, 2021, and 2023 waves

denominator.unit: individuals interviewed in the 2025 representative survey; published percentages refer to the survey population

cinema_2016.unit: percent attending cinema at least once a year in 2016

cinema_2025.unit: percent attending cinema at least once a year in 2025

library_2025.value: stabilized at levels similar to before the pandemic

mechanism.value: Post-pandemic cultural recovery is venue-specific: repeated public-service use can stabilize while cinema attendance remains below its earlier baseline

observations.method: Statistics Norway repeated Cultural Barometer survey; the 2025 wave interviewed a representative sample and compares participation with prior survey years.
observations.uncertainty: The article does not provide the full instrument, subgroup estimates, ticket prices, venue supply, digital substitution, or individual-level panel transitions; cross-wave differences are descriptive and may reflect changing survey conditions as well as behavior.
observations.subgroup: Norwegian population represented by the 2025 survey; children and young people are separately identified as high users of cultural activities.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower annual cinema rate may reflect changing film access or release patterns rather than a general decline in cultural engagement; library stabilization may coexist with changes in intensity or purpose of use.

observations.period: 2025 Cultural Barometer; venue and age patterns

denominator.unit: individuals interviewed in the 2025 representative survey; activity percentages refer to the survey population

children_library.unit: approximately percent of children aged 9-15 visiting a library within a year

mechanism.value: Age and venue structure matter: children sustain high library use while adult theatre attendance falls and festivals remain a substantial participatory route

observations.method: Statistics Norway survey estimates for cultural attendance, with the article's reported cross-year and age comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: The public article does not provide all age-by-venue cells, frequency distributions, socioeconomic gradients, or reasons for change; the children’s estimate is rounded in the narrative.
observations.subgroup: Children aged 9-15 compared with the wider population; adults and children may have different survey instruments and activity opportunities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional access through schools, families, or local libraries may explain child library use without implying equivalent independent cultural agency or later adult continuity.

observations.period: 2025 Cultural Barometer; desired participation and barriers

denominator.unit: individuals interviewed in the 2025 representative survey; desire shares refer to respondents reporting the relevant cultural offer

wish_more_concerts.unit: percent wishing to attend concerts more often

wish_more_cinema.unit: percent wishing to attend cinema more often

wish_more_libraries.unit: percent wishing to visit libraries more often

barriers.value: financial reasons, lack of time, and more interesting alternatives were the most common barriers among people wanting more cultural participation

mechanism.value: Unmet cultural demand is jointly constrained by money, time, and competing attention rather than by simple lack of interest

observations.method: Statistics Norway survey question on desired additional attendance and reported barriers.
observations.uncertainty: The article does not publish the full barrier percentages, causal ordering, event prices, travel time, or whether people later converted desire into attendance.
observations.subgroup: Respondents expressing a desire to attend cultural offerings more frequently; no causal subgroup model is reported.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stated desire may reflect aspirational preferences or social norms; competing options can be another form of cultural participation rather than a barrier to culture overall.

related_sources.claim: Statistics Norway publication page provides the sample, response rate, repeated-wave framing, activity estimates, and barriers summary.
Statistics Norway culture and recreation statistics landing page provides the source-family context for the Cultural Barometer.

boundary: This record adds repeated, representative cultural-participation evidence from Norway. It supports venue-specific post-pandemic stabilization, age differences, and unmet-demand barriers, not a causal pandemic effect, universal cultural recovery, price elasticity, digital substitution, or individual-level persistence.
